title: Rethinking Rubric Generation for LLM Judges and Reward Models
note: The paper that gave me RLNR. It splits vague criteria until they bite and fires the ones that reward the weaker draft. Every writers' room does this; now it is a training signal.

title: Retell, Reward, Repeat
note: The only paper so far that put a narratology book (Todorov) into the reward. Closest thing to my retelling test, and the first I will try to beat.

title: StoryAlign: Evaluating and Training Reward Models for Story Generation
note: Finds that reward models prefer machine-written stories to human ones. That bias is the whole problem in one table.

title: LitBench
who: Fein, Russo, Xiang et al., Stanford
note: The reference dataset. The best judge agrees with humans 73 percent of the time; the gap is where structure has to do the work.

title: Art or Artifice? The Torrance Test of Creative Writing
note: Fourteen tests written with expert writers. Model stories passed three to ten times fewer of them. Read it as a craftsperson, not as a benchmark.

title: POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories
note: A 9B model, four A100s, competitive long fiction. The budget that makes Beatcode possible on a residency's income.

title: Rubric Curriculum RL
note: A moving rubric is harder to hack than a fixed one. Useful for anyone who has watched a writer learn to game the note.

title: RLMR: Reinforcement Learning with Mixed Rewards
note: Half the reward is a judge, half is a verifier, and the mix moves per sample. The closest existing design to the one I want to build.

title: NCP-Bench: Narrative Commitment Preservation
note: Checks an interactive story turn by turn against a ledger of facts and commitments. A commitment ledger is a beat graph by another name.

title: Narrative Flattening
who: Li, Zhu, Wu, Bao, Evans, Chicago
note: Measures how post-training compresses stories toward one mundane regime. The scientific version of what I called slop in Understanding Taste.
